title: The project starts
note:
This began as an idea for a 32X port. The complaints people have about the game are mostly about its design (deaths with little warning, restarting floors, fights that play alike), and the 32X wouldn't fix those, so it's now a straight patch for the Genesis version. The three goals are fairness, bug fixes, and smoother performance where that's possible.

The target is The Immortal (USA, Europe), 1 MB, serial T-50186. Its checksum is correct and its header declares no save RAM. Nothing in the game has been examined or changed yet.

The game's screenshots and clips will appear here but stay out of git, so they only show on the machine that made them.

title: The game runs under test, and the first findings
note:
The game now runs headless with scripted input, and a profiling build of PicoDrive shows where its time goes. All eight levels can be reached directly.

The game updates once every 5 video frames, 12 times a second. In random walks 23% of those updates came late, and about half on level 6. On levels 5 and 6 the late ones spend much longer building object graphics. On levels 2, 4 and 8 the cause is still unknown. These timings are from the emulator.

Three lives per level is confirmed. After the third death the game offers a new game from the very first room, or asks for a certificate, even though it already has a way to reload a level without one.

Details are in docs/how-the-game-works.md. The picture shows the eight levels and stays on this machine.

title: BlastEm agrees with PicoDrive
note:
The same scripted runs now work on BlastEm, a much more exacting emulator. Across all eight levels 23.0% of the game's updates ran late on both, and level by level the figures match within a point, apart from level 2, where the random walks end early at deaths and prompts. The 4-frame gaps PicoDrive showed don't appear on BlastEm, so they look like a PicoDrive quirk.

PicoDrive stays in use for profiling, and BlastEm becomes the check on whether an optimization really helps. None of this has been run on a real Genesis yet.
